title: Which of these seven decimals stand for the same number?
description: Seven decimals such as 4.5, 4.05 and 04.50 are sorted into groups that stand for the same number by stripping the outer zeroes. Keeko doubts the middle zero and thinks 4.05 equals 4.5.
teaching_notes: One idea: zeroes at the right end of the decimal part and the left end of the whole part can be dropped, but a zero in the middle holds a place. Watch for students who drop every zero.

source: Which of these are the same: 4.5, 4.05, 0.405, 4.050, 4.50,
video_script.why: The child knows a right-end zero adds nothing and now sorts several decimals with zeros in different places.
video_script.substitution: Strip the zeroes at the outer ends of each decimal, then compare what is left.
video_script.anchor: the seven decimals of the book: 4.5, 4.05, 0.405, 4.050, 4.50, 4.005 and 04.50
video_script.wrong_answer: is the same as four point five
video_script.wrong_move: Drops the zero in the middle of 4.05 and says it equals 4.5.
video_script.payoff_line: Strip the outer zeroes and keep the middle ones

final_answer.spoken: four point five, four point five zero and zero four point five zero are equal; four point zero five and four point zero five zero are equal; zero point four zero five and four point zero zero five stand alone

maths_rules: 04.50 = 4.5 after stripping the left-end zero and the right-end zero
4.05 has 0 tenths, 4.5 has 5 tenths, so they differ
0.405 and 4.005 differ from all the others
video_script.design: The seven decimals sit in a row. Outer zeroes fade out one by one; middle zeroes stay and glow.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; seven decimals in a row: 4.5, 4.05, 0.405, 4.050, 4.50, 4.005, 04.50
narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about seven decimals.
<bookmark mark='first'/>Four point five, four point zero five, and zero point four zero five.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Four point zero five zero, four point five zero, and four point zero zero five.
<bookmark mark='last'/>The last is zero four point five zero. Which of these are the same?

beats.on_screen: the seven decimals stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits beside the row of decimals

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: outer zeroes: right end of the decimal part, left end of the whole part

marks.outer: the two kinds of outer zero are outlined
marks.mid: a middle zero is outlined in another colour

narration: <bookmark mark='outer'/>A zero at the right end of the decimal part adds nothing. A zero at the left end of the whole part adds nothing.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>A zero in the middle holds a place, so it stays.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the seven decimals in the row.

beats.on_screen: To find: which decimals stand for the same number
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find which ones stand for the same number.

marks.a: the zero at the end of four point five zero fades
marks.b: both outer zeroes of zero four point five zero fade

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, strip the zeroes at the outer ends.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Four point five zero loses its last zero and becomes four point five.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Zero four point five zero loses both outer zeroes and also becomes four point five.

marks.eq: the three decimals are joined by equal signs

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step two, group the first set. Four point five, four point five zero, and zero four point five zero are equal.

marks.strip: the zero at the end of four point zero five zero fades

narration: <bookmark mark='strip'/>Step three, four point zero five zero loses its last zero and becomes four point zero five.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>These two are equal.

beats.on_screen: 0.405 and 4.005 have no outer zeroes to strip; they differ from the rest

marks.alone: zero point four zero five and four point zero zero five move to one side
marks.why: their digits differ in the units place and the tenths place

narration: <bookmark mark='alone'/>Step four, look at zero point four zero five and four point zero zero five. They have no outer zeroes to strip.
<bookmark mark='why'/>They differ from all the others, so each stands alone.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Strip the outer zeroes and keep the middle ones.
<bookmark mark='g1'/>Four point five, four point five zero and zero four point five zero are equal.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Four point zero five and four point zero five zero are equal. The other two stand alone.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the row of decimals
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: a speech bubble: 4.05 = 4.5; 4.05 has 0 tenths, 4.5 has 5 tenths; the bubble is crossed out

marks.fix: the tenths place of each decimal is shown

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks four point zero five is the same as four point five. Keeko says a zero is only a zero.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But four point zero five has no tenths, while four point five has five tenths.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>A zero in the middle holds a place, so it cannot be removed.
